subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 26, 2026.
Today we will review 2 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Ringer's lactate versus saline in the fluids in septic shock (
sentences: Story 1 is about Ringer's lactate versus saline in the fluids in septic shock (FISSH) trial: a multicentre, blinded, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial..
This is a recent research article from The Lancet. Respiratory medicine.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in adults (aged ≥16 years) at 30 academic and community hospitals across Canada and Saudi Arabia who were critically ill with septic shock were randomly assigned (1:1) via a web-based rand, how should we interpret Ringer's lactate compared with saline in the fluids in septic shock (FISSH) trial: a multicentre, blinded, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial?

Between Oct 6, 2018, and Feb 1, 2026, we screened 2457 patients and randomly assigned 1113, with a further ten excluded after randomisation (557 patients in the Ringer's lactate group and 546 in the saline group).
491 (44·5%) were female and 612 (55·5%) were male, the mean baseline APACHE II score was 24·7 (SD 8·8), and patients received a mean of 5844 mL (SD 4761) of study fluid.
187 (33·6%) patients died in the Ringer's lactate group 180 (33·0%) died in the saline group (relative risk 1·02 [95% CI 0·86-1·21]; p=0·80).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.

The bedside implication is this: This is relevant to default ICU fluid choice; focus on absolute mortality difference, kidney outcomes, and whether the enrolled population matches your resuscitation patients.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Story 2 - Telehealth to Support Coordinated Spontaneous Awakening and Br
sentences: Story 2 is about Telehealth to Support Coordinated Spontaneous Awakening and Breathing Trials in Invasive Ventilation: The TEACH Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial..
This is a randomized / clinical trial from JAMA.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in Patients aged 16 years or older who were intubated and mechanically ventilated in the intensive care unit were enrolled from December 1, 2022, until July 31, 2025, with last follow-up on, how should we interpret ntervention added to a standard audit and feedback implementation of C-SAT/SBT increases adherence and improves outcomes compared with standard audit and feedback implementation alone (control). A cluster randomized type 2 hybrid effectiveness-implementat?
There were 4544 patients at telehealth hospitals, 6438 patients at control hospitals, and 1789 preimplementation common baseline patients (median [IQR] age, 62 [47-71] years; 4826 [37.8%] female).

The baseline C-SAT/SBT adherence rate of 43.9% increased to 90.3% at telehealth intervention hospitals and to 77.6% at control hospitals (odds ratio for change in telehealth vs change in control, 2.87; 1-sided 95% lower confidence limit, 2.44; P < .001; absolute difference, 11.4%; 95% CI, 8.8%-14.3%).

Median (IQR) ventilator-free days from a common baseline of 24 (0-26) increased to 25 (10-27) at telehealth intervention hospitals and 25 (1-27) at control hospitals (odds ratio for change in telehealth vs change in control, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.01-1.45, P = .04; absolute difference, 1.02 days; 95% CI, 0.05-1.96 days).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use this for journal club before practice change; decide whether the measured outcome is important enough for bedside decisions.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Ringer's lactate versus saline in the fluids in septic shock (FISSH) trial: a multicentre, blinded, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial.
articles.summary: In this multicentre, blinded, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial, adults (aged ≥16 years) at 30 academic and community hospitals across Canada and Saudi Arabia who were critically ill with septic shock were randomly assigned (1:1) via a web-based randomisation system to receive Ringer's lactate or 0·9% saline for all bolus and maintenance fluid throughout their intensive care unit (ICU) stay up to day 30, stratified by hospital. We included patients who had a systolic blood pressure lower than 90 mm Hg or a mean arterial pressure of less than 65 mm Hg after 1 L bolus or a serum lactate greater than 4 mmol/L, had a clinically suspected infection, and were within 6 h of emergency department presentation or ICU consultation. We excluded patients who had new raised intracranial pressure, had acute burn injury on more than 10% of the body surface area, were already receiving chronic or acute dialysis at the time of screening, or were admitted to ICU directly from the operating room, post-anaesthetic care unit, or another hospital or health-care facility. Between Oct 6, 2018, and Feb 1, 2026, we screened 2457 patients and randomly assigned 1113, with a further ten excluded after randomisation (557 patients in the Ringer's lactate group and 546 in the saline group). 491 (44·5%) were female and 612 (55·5%) were male, the mean baseline APACHE II score was 24·7 (SD 8·8), and patients received a mean of 5844 mL (SD 4761) of study fluid.

articles.title: Telehealth to Support Coordinated Spontaneous Awakening and Breathing Trials in Invasive Ventilation: The TEACH Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: Patients aged 16 years or older who were intubated and mechanically ventilated in the intensive care unit were enrolled from December 1, 2022, until July 31, 2025, with last follow-up on January 23, 2026. C-SAT/SBT was defined as any day that the SAT and SBT were separately adherent, and the SAT followed the SBT within 2 hours or both occurred before noon, or the patient was extubated. There were 4544 patients at telehealth hospitals, 6438 patients at control hospitals, and 1789 preimplementation common baseline patients (median [IQR] age, 62 [47-71] years; 4826 [37.8%] female). The baseline C-SAT/SBT adherence rate of 43.9% increased to 90.3% at telehealth intervention hospitals and to 77.6% at control hospitals (odds ratio for change in telehealth vs change in control, 2.87; 1-sided 95% lower confidence limit, 2.44; P < .001; absolute difference, 11.4%; 95% CI, 8.8%-14.3%). Median (IQR) ventilator-free days from a common baseline of 24 (0-26) increased to 25 (10-27) at telehealth intervention hospitals and 25 (1-27) at control hospitals (odds ratio for change in telehealth vs change in control, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.01-1.45, P = .04; absolute difference, 1.02 days; 95% CI, 0.05-1.96 days).
